pat.title: BLEA Entrance PAT (pass/fail gate)
form: Push-up: body straight, go down until upper arms are parallel and chest compresses the foam block, lock arms out at the top.
Sit-up: fingers interlocked behind head, elbows touch knees, shoulder blades return to the mat.
Squat thrust: hands to floor, kick both feet back together to a straight plank, feet back in, stand fully with arms overhead.
Rep standards above are as published by WSCJTC/NTN. Confirm with the FWPD proctor which standard they score against.

vswat.title: VSWAT Fitness Assessment (ranked)
form: Rep standards for pull-ups (kip vs. strict), burpees (chest to floor? jump?) and deadlift lockout are not given in the announcement. Ask a current Valley SWAT member or the test proctor. Until then, train strict pull-ups and chest-to-floor burpees.
Deadlift load = 75% of YOUR weigh-in body weight. If you lose 10 lb the bar drops to about 127.5 lb. Train at 135 lb either way.

pacing: 10-min AMRAP: the pull-ups set your pace. From round 1, break them before failure (3-2, then 2-2-1 later). One failed rep costs more time than a planned break.
Push-ups: sets of 6-4 or 5-5 from the start. Never take a set to failure in rounds 1-4.
Air squats: always unbroken. Breathe in through the nose on the squats and use them to recover.
Pick a target round time from your baseline (e.g. 75 s/round = 8 rounds) and hold it ±5 s. Check the clock every round. If rounds 1-2 are more than 10 s faster than target, you went out too hot.
3-min DL/burpee: deadlifts touch-and-go, reset the grip only if needed. Burpees at a smooth, steady rhythm, ~2.5-3 s each. Walk to the bar, don't rest at it. Target ≈ 25-30 s/round = 6-7 rounds.
The 3:00 rests: walk the first 60 s, take nasal breaths, chalk up, set up at the bar with 20 s left.
The second DL/burpee AMRAP is where rankings are decided. Plan to match or beat your first-AMRAP score.

pullup_levels.prescription: Band-assisted pull-ups 5×5 (band light enough that rep 5 is hard) + 3×3 eccentric negatives (jump up, 5 s lower) + 3×20 s flexed-arm hang + inverted rows 3×8-10.
pullup_levels.gtg: Negatives: 3-5 singles spread across the day

pullup_levels.prescription: 6 sets × (max − 1, min 1) strict, 2:00 rest, + band-assisted back-off 2×6 + 3×3 negatives.
8 sets × 50-60% of max (e.g. max 8 → 8×4), 90 s rest. Finish with 1 set of dead hang to failure.
EMOM 10: 5 strict pull-ups (test-standard reps). Add 10 lb in a backpack once all 10 minutes are clean.

deadlift_cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins about 1 in from the bar.
Hinge down and grip just outside the legs. Shins come to the bar. Chest up, 'bend the bar' to engage the lats.
Big breath into the belly, brace, push the floor away. Hips and shoulders rise together.
Lock out with glutes, not by leaning back. Lower by sending the hips back first, bar close to the legs.
Stop the set if your lower back rounds or the bar drifts forward. Technique comes before load in week 1.
For the test, use touch-and-go reps (no bouncing) and a double-overhand grip as long as it holds, then switch to mixed grip.

RAMP-12: 2 rounds: 5/side world's greatest stretch · 10 glute bridges · 15 band pull-aparts · 10 scap pull-ups (or 20 s dead hang) · 10 pause air squats · 5 inchworm-to-push-up
Specific: 2 × 3 pull-ups (or band) · 2 × 5 push-ups · 2 × 5 squat thrusts, building speed
RAMP-8: 1 round: 5/side world's greatest stretch · 10 glute bridges · 15 band pull-aparts · 10 air squats · 20 s dead hang

P1.name: Kickoff: movement school + Zone 2
blocks: Push-ups: 3 × 8 at PAT standard (film one set from the side)
PAT sit-ups: 3 × 10, fingers interlocked behind head, elbows to knees
Squat thrusts: 3 × 8, practice a straight plank and full stand
Zone 2 walk/jog 25 min: you should be able to speak full sentences (≈120-140 bpm)
P1.scale: If you're stiff after the shift, swap the jog for a brisk walk.

P2.name: Thanksgiving (adjusted): engine + pull + core
blocks: You trained Wednesday before shift: push-ups, sit-ups, squat thrusts and Zone 2. Today skips those patterns so Sunday's baseline is fresh.
Then 6 × 20 s hill or stair strides at ~85%, walk back down to recover
Pull-ups 5 × 3 (band or slow negatives if needed), 2 min rest, stop 2+ reps short of failure
Hips, T-spine, shoulders: 5 picks, about 8 min
P2.scale: Crisp, not crushing. No push-ups, sit-ups or squat thrusts today. Sunday's max-effort baseline matters more.

P3.name: Pre-week: Mobility + Zone 2
P3.scale: Easy day. You should finish feeling better than when you started.

P4.name: Post-shift: easy walk + setup
blocks: 30-min easy walk in daylight (resets the body clock)
P4.scale: Rest day. Install the pull-up bar and test it.

S0.name: BASELINE TEST DAY: PAT + VSWAT
blocks: Weigh in on waking (log it) + resting HR
Set up timer app, a partner to count reps if possible, and phone video of one set per event
1 all-out set, dead hang to chin over bar. Log the reps → this sets your pull-up level (L0-L3)
2. BLEA PAT, official order and rests
Push-ups 90 s: keep going past 20 and record the MAX
Stop at the heaviest load where all 5 reps are clean (neutral back) and log it
10:00 AMRAP 5 pull-ups / 10 push-ups / 15 air squats (use a band if you have <3 strict and log the band)
Rest 3:00 → 3:00 AMRAP 5 DL @135 (or your clean load) / 5 burpees
Log rounds + extra reps for each part
10-min walk + full mobility. Eat Meal 2 within 45 min
S0.scale: This is your 'before' picture. Give honest maximal effort with perfect standards. Skip a part only for pain (not discomfort).

S1.name: Strength A + Engine
blocks: 3 s lowering on rep 1 of each set · rest 2:00
Re-read the deadlift cues before set 1
B1 Pull-ups: use your LEVEL prescription
B2 Push-ups: 5 sets × 60% of PAT max (strict), rest 90 s after the pair
C1 Goblet squat 3 × 12 (or air squat 3 × 20 with a 2 s pause)
Zone 2 30:00 bike / rower / incline treadmill, HR ≈ 120-140 or nasal-breathing only
S1.scale: If the back is fatigued, cut deadlifts to 3 sets. Never trade form for 135 this week.

S2.name: PAT Power + Intervals (pre-shift)
blocks: 5 sets × 50% of PAT max, strict to standard, 60 s rest
4 sets × 50% of PAT max, 60 s rest, fingers interlocked, elbows to knees
8 reps every minute (scale 6, push to 10 if easy). The test pace is ~12/min, so build up to it
8 × (0:30 hard @ RPE 8 / 1:30 easy) on bike or rower
S2.scale: First shift night tonight. Cap the intervals at 6 if you slept less than 7 h.

S3.name: Engine + Pull Volume (pre-shift)
blocks: 35:00 continuous at conversational pace. Log avg HR (this should drop over the weeks)
Pull-ups: 5 sets × 50% max (or band 5×5) · 90 s rest
S3.scale: Hard work at low intensity. If you're wrecked from last night, do the Zone 2 work and only half the pull volume.

S4.name: VSWAT Practice: pacing rehearsal (pre-shift)
blocks: Use the baseline round time minus 3 s as your split. Break pull-ups 3-2 from round 1
3:00 rest between · touch-and-go DL · steady burpee rhythm
S4.scale: Hold about 85% effort. Today is for pacing practice, not a max test.

S5.name: Recovery + Mobility (pre-shift)
blocks: GTG: 3 easy pull-up sets (well short of failure)
S5.scale: Fourth night shift in a row. Do the minimum here, and show up for it.

S6.name: Strength B (post-shift)
blocks: 5 × 3 @ 135 if Monday's sets were crisp, otherwise your clean load. Explode off the floor · rest 2:00
Pull-up ladder 1-2-3 (L0: band 2-3-4) · Push-up ladder 5-10-15 · rest 2:00 between ladders
C2 Farmer carry 40 yd heavy DBs (grip for DL/pull-ups)
5 burpees each minute in ≤15 s, smooth and chest to floor
S6.scale: FATIGUE RULE: if you slept under 5 h or resting HR is 10+ bpm over baseline, do 3 sets each and skip D.

S7.name: Week-1 Checkpoint: PAT mock + Zone 2
blocks: Push-ups 90 s (max) → 3:00 → Sit-ups 90 s (max) → 5:00 → Squat thrusts 3:00 (max)
Log it and compare with baseline
S7.scale: You'll shoot live fire after this. Keep the Zone 2 truly easy so your hands are steady.

F1.name: On-shift flex: Zone 2 + mobility (only if calls allow)
blocks: Stay radio-up with your gear staged by the door. Drop it the second a call comes.
Keep it easy (Zone 2). You have to be able to go straight to a hot call.
30-40 min Zone 2 bike/rower/incline walk at conversational pace
F1.scale: SKIP RULE: if calls stack up, skip it. Don't make it up later or push it past 04:00. The pre-shift session already counted.

F2.name: On-shift flex: mobility + pull-up practice (low fatigue)
blocks: Radio-up, gear staged. Low fatigue only, because tomorrow is a hard session.
4 sets of pull-ups at ≤ 50% of max
F2.scale: SKIP RULE: optional. Skip it if you're busy or beat up.

daily_anchors.text: No caffeine within 6 h of sleep

targets: 3 meals + 1 Huel shake a day. Carbs go in the meals before and after training
≈ 2,300 kcal on training days · ≈ 2,200 on recovery days (docx range 2,200-2,400)
≈ 180-200 g (docx 170-180 minimum), about 45-65 g per meal + 40 g from the shake
≈ 220 g, with ~70% in the pre- and post-training meals
Lose 0.5-1.0 lb/week. If you're losing more than 1.5 lb/week for 2 weeks or your performance drops, add 150 kcal of carbs. Performance comes first
3.5 L baseline + 0.5-0.75 L per training hour. Patrol car: one 1 L bottle + electrolytes in the cooler, refill at the station. Taper off 60 min before sleep
≤ 400 mg/day. Shift nights: last dose by 01:00 (6 h before 07:30 sleep)
supplements: 5 g daily, every day. Mix it into the Huel shake so it can't be forgotten
1 serving/day as the shake (~400 kcal / 40 g protein per docx). Keep powder pre-measured in a shaker in the cooler bag
Per docx: continue if tolerated. Check the label with your physician
1 packet on shift nights and after long Zone 2 sessions

shift.name: Shift day (Tue-Fri): sleep 07:30-14:30, train ~16:00 at home
meals: Overnight protein oats jar + 3 egg bites
7 oz chili-lime chicken + 1½ cups rice + broccoli
Turkey burrito bowl (eat cold or microwave at the station) OR beef chili in a food thermos + apple
Huel Black + 5 g creatine in a shaker
shift.total: ≈ 2,300 kcal · ≈ 200 P. Nothing heavy after 04:00 or before day sleep

off.name: Off day (Sat-Mon)
meals: 3 eggs + 1 cup egg whites scramble w/ spinach, ½ cup (dry) oats + berries
Turkey burrito bowl + 1 cup rice + green beans
6 oz salmon (or 1 bowl chili) + roasted sweet potato + salad · Greek yogurt + berries for dessert

rules: Patrol: everything you eat on shift has to work cold, in one hand, or come out of a thermos. No meals that need plating.
If a call wipes out the shift meal, have the shake first and eat the bowl when you can. Don't skip both.
Can't eat the plan? Plate rule: 2 palms of protein, 1-2 fists of carbs (more on training days), 2 fists of vegetables.
Thanksgiving: walk first, protein first, one plate, one dessert slice.
Food safety (USDA): cooked meat keeps 3-4 days in the fridge. The Thu-Sun portions get frozen on prep day and thawed in the fridge the night before.

recipes.name: Overnight protein oats
ing: 200 g rolled oats (½ cup + 2 tbsp per jar)
680 g plain 0% Greek yogurt (¾ cup per jar)
steps: In each jar: 50 g oats, 170 g yogurt, 1 tbsp chia, 100 g berries, cinnamon, splash of milk.
Stir, lid, refrigerate. Good for 4-5 days.

recipes.name: Egg bites (muffin tin)
ing: 1 cup chopped spinach, ½ bell pepper, ¼ onion
steps: Oven 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs and whites, then stir in the veg.
Fill the cups ¾ full and top with cheese.
Bake 20-22 min. Cool, then refrigerate. Keeps 5 days.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan chili-lime chicken
recipes.makes: 5 portions of 7 oz cooked (Tue-Fri dinners + 1 spare)
ing: 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1½ tsp salt
steps: Oven 425°F. Butterfly thick breasts so they cook evenly.
Toss with oil, lime and spices.
Roast 18-22 min to 165°F inside. Rest 5 min, then slice.
Portion into 5 containers with 1½ cups rice + broccoli. Fridge 2 (Tue, Wed), freeze 3 (Thu, Fri, spare).
recipes.macro: per 7 oz chicken ≈ 330 kcal · 62 g protein

recipes.name: Turkey burrito bowls
ing: Rice (from the batch) + frozen green beans
steps: Brown the turkey and drain.
Add peppers and onion, cook 5 min.
Stir in beans, salsa and seasoning, simmer 10 min.
Bowls: turkey mix + ¾-1 cup rice + green beans. Use leak-proof containers. These are eaten in the patrol car, cold or microwaved.
Fridge 2 (Mon lunch, Tue shift), freeze 4.

recipes.name: Lean beef & bean chili (thermos meal)
recipes.makes: 6 bowls (2 shift meals + 1 dinner + 3 frozen for next week)
ing: 2 cans (15 oz) kidney or pinto beans
2 tbsp chili powder, 1 tbsp cumin, salt
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and garlic.
Add everything else and simmer 30 min.
Portion into 6. Fridge 1, freeze 5.
Shift nights: heat until steaming. Pre-heat the thermos with boiling water for 5 min, dump it, then fill with chili.

recipes.name: Rice, sweet potatoes & veg
ing: 4 cups dry jasmine rice (≈ 12 cups cooked)
steps: Rice cooker: 4 cups rice.
Roast the sweet potato at 425°F for 30 min.
Roast the broccoli at 425°F for 15-18 min.
Green beans go straight into the turkey bowls frozen (they thaw in the fridge).
recipes.macro: 1 cup rice ≈ 205 kcal · 200 g sweet potato ≈ 180 kcal

recipes.name: Salmon (cook the day of)
ing: 2 × 6 oz salmon fillets (frozen bag is fine)
steps: Fresh: cook within 2 days (Monday's). Frozen: thaw in the fridge overnight (Saturday's).
Air fryer at 400°F for 8-10 min, or oven at 425°F for 12 min.

grocery: Salmon fillets: 2 × 6 oz (or a frozen bag)
Jasmine rice: 2 lb bag (4 cups used)
Black beans: 1 can · Kidney or pinto beans: 2 cans
Spices: chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, low-sodium taco seasoning, cinnamon
Wheat bread: 1 loaf (Fri shift sandwich, if needed)
Food thermos 16-24 oz + insulated lunch cooler + ice pack (one-time)
gear: Doorway pull-up bar + loop resistance bands (light/medium/heavy)
Shot-timer app with a PAR mode (or a real shot timer) + interval timer app
Snap caps/dummy rounds for the duty pistol AND rifle (inert, colored)
Dry-fire target: 1/3-scale or reduced IPSC/B-8 taped on a safe backstop wall
Gym access with a barbell + 2 × 45 lb plates (135 lb) and a pull-up bar
Blackout curtains/eye mask + earplugs/white noise for day sleep
Body-weight scale. Weigh daily on waking and track the 7-day average

safety: Use a dedicated dry-fire area with a backstop that would stop a round (exterior wall/body-armor panel/bookcase), never a wall people are behind.
Unload: drop the magazine, lock the slide/bolt open, check the chamber visually AND physically. Check it twice.
NO LIVE AMMUNITION IN THE ROOM. Put all magazines and loose rounds in another room, locked. Use only inert dummy rounds in a different color.
Say it out loud: 'This is dry practice. The weapon is unloaded.' Set a timer to bound the session (15-20 min).
When you finish, say: 'Dry practice is over.' Do NOT do 'one more rep' after reloading. Reload in a different room and holster immediately.
Follow FWPD firearms policy for dry practice with duty weapons. If you're unsure, use a SIRT/blue gun for draws and a duty-identical training gun for manipulations.
par_table: Pistol: draw → first shot (7 yd, A-zone)
Drills 1 & 5: 6 rds in 5 s at 7 yd needs ≈ 1.5 s draw + 0.6 splits live
Drill 3: 6 rds in 10 s with a reload
Drill 2: 7 rds in 15 s with one malfunction
Pistol: draw → 1st shot STRONG hand only
Drill 6: 12 rds in 15 s (2H head / SHO / WHO)
Pistol: transfer to WEAK hand → shot
Carbine: low ready → first shot (25 yd)
Carbine: shoulder transition with SAFE on/off
Drill 3: 10 rds in 18 s, dummy + reload
Drill 6: 2 rifle + 1 pistol to head in 5 s

DF0.name: Dry-fire setup + baseline times
reps: Run the full safety protocol and set up the station
10 slow-motion draws (5 s each), smooth and perfect
Use the shot timer: 5 draw → first shot, 5 reloads, 5 tap-racks. Log your BEST and AVERAGE times as the baseline

DF1.name: Pistol draw & recoil-control mechanics (Drills 1, 5)
reps: 10 slow draws (3 s), then 10 at a natural pace with no timer
20 draw → 1 press at PAR 2.0 s (Sun target 1.7 s), on a reduced 7-yd target
10 draw → 'two-press' (press, reset, press), focusing on the reset
Finish: 5 perfect slow reps

DF2.name: Malfunctions + reloads (Drills 2, 3)
reps: Load a mag with 1 inert dummy. 10 × tap-rack → press at PAR 1.6 s
10 × slide-lock (empty mag) reload → press at PAR 3.0 s
5 × from the holster: draw → press → 'click' → tap-rack → press
Stage practice: mags in the exact carrier positions you'll use at selection

DF3.name: Strong/weak hand + head box (Drill 6)
reps: 10 × draw → 4 presses on a head box (reset each press)
10 × strong-hand-only presses from compressed ready (PAR 2.6 s from the holster)
10 × transfer to the weak hand → press (PAR 2.4 s). Cant if that's what you train
3 × full Drill 6 sequence dry, 15 s par (12 presses)

DF4.name: Carbine: mount, shoulder transitions, SAFE (Carbine Drills 2, 3)
reps: 15 × low ready → mount → press at PAR 1.3 s, safe off on the mount, SAFE ON before lowering
10 × strong → SAFE → support shoulder → off safe → press (PAR 2.5 s)
10 × dummy in the mag → malfunction clear → press, and 5 × reload → press (PAR 3.5 s)

DF5.name: Movement + transitions (Pistol Drill 4, Carbine Drills 4, 6)
reps: Hallway SOM: from ready, heel-toe walk forward 4-5 steps doing 5 body presses + 1 head (PAR 6 s pistol, 7 s carbine)
10 × carbine 2 presses on the head → transition (dead trigger/click) → draw → 1 press on the head (PAR 2.0 s)
Notice whether the sights move when you step, and smooth the walk out

DF6.name: Dry run of the FULL pistol course
reps: Run Pistol Drills 1-6 dry against the official time limits, with dummy rounds for Drills 2 and 3
Write down which drill felt hardest. That becomes next week's focus
3 × draw → press at PAR 1.7 s to close

live.title: Live fire: VSWAT courses under the clock (Sun 12/6)
logistics: Range needs 50 yd (carbine) + room to move 15→7 and 10→3 yd. FWPD range/open range day or a public range that allows draw + movement (confirm first)
Bring: duty pistol + carbine, 6 pistol mags, 4 rifle mags, 10 pistol & 5 rifle dummy rounds, IPSC/B-8 + head targets, shot timer, pasters/marker, score sheet (Logs tab), partner to set dummies/count
plan: 5 × 5 at 7 yd slow fire for a group, then 3 draw-and-1 (no timer)
Shoot it exactly as written. Partner randomizes the dummy + the short mag. Score it
Repeat that drill 3-5× with the timer
Score it. Compare against 32 (VSWAT min) / 28 (FW new officer min)
live.scoring: Score per drill: hits, misses, rounds over time. Points = hits − over-time rounds (1-pt penalty each). Any miss = fails the 100%-hits requirement. Confirm zone scoring (body/head boxes) with VSWAT range staff, since the course sheet doesn't define the zones.

pistol: From holster, draw and fire 3 rds
Dummy randomly in first 5 rds; draw, fire 7 total
First mag random <4 rds; draw, fire 6 total
Draw: 4 head 2H, 4 body SHO, 4 body WHO
carbine: 3 body strong side + 3 body support side; SAFE when transitioning
Mag preset: 1 dummy + up to 7 live; fire 10 (malf + speed reload)
SOM: 5 body + 1 head, all before the 7-yd line
Rifle loaded with 2: 2 head (rifle), transition, 1 head (pistol)
courses.rules: 40 rds / 40 pts. 100% hits required. Min 80% (32 pts) · FW NEW SWAT OFFICER min 70% (28 pts). Each round fired over time = −1 pt. FWPD pistol + rifle quals are pass/fail (≤ 2 attempts); VSWAT courses are one attempt and ranked.

cases.name: Graham v. Connor
cases.holding: All claims that officers used excessive force during an arrest, investigatory stop or other seizure are analyzed under the Fourth Amendment's 'objective reasonableness' standard, not substantive due process. Reasonableness is judged from the perspective of a reasonable officer on the scene, not with 20/20 hindsight, and allows for split-second judgments in tense, uncertain and rapidly evolving situations. The officer's subjective intent is irrelevant.
cases.factors: The three Graham factors: (1) severity of the crime at issue, (2) whether the suspect poses an immediate threat to the safety of officers or others, (3) whether the suspect is actively resisting or attempting to evade arrest by flight.
cases.swat: Every use-of-force articulation in a SWAT report or interview has to map to Graham. Fast-moving entries are the 'tense, uncertain, rapidly evolving' setting the Court described, but WA's RCW 10.120 adds 'necessary' + reasonable care on top of Graham.
cases.quiz: Name the three Graham factors and the vantage point a court must use.
cases.answer: Severity of the crime, immediate threat, active resistance/flight. Judged as a reasonable officer on scene, without hindsight, allowing for split-second decisions.

cases.name: Tennessee v. Garner
cases.holding: Using deadly force to prevent escape is a Fourth Amendment seizure. It may not be used unless it is necessary to prevent the escape AND the officer has probable cause to believe the suspect poses a significant threat of death or serious physical injury to the officer or others. Where feasible, some warning must be given. The Court held the Tennessee statute unconstitutional as applied to an unarmed, non-dangerous fleeing burglary suspect.
cases.swat: This governs fleeing-felon situations on perimeters and containment, e.g. a 'squirter' leaving a target house. WA adds RCW 9A.16.040 (criminal) and RCW 10.120.020(2) (civil 'immediate threat' standard), and FWPD adopts all three (MOS 4.1.3).
cases.quiz: When may deadly force be used against a fleeing suspect under Garner? What about a warning?
cases.answer: Only if necessary to prevent escape and there's probable cause the suspect poses a significant threat of death/serious injury to officers or others. Give a warning where feasible.

cases.name: Barnes v. Felix
cases.holding: The Court was unanimous (May 15, 2025). It rejected the Fifth Circuit's 'moment-of-threat' rule, which looked only at the instant the officer was in danger. Excessive-force claims get a totality-of-the-circumstances analysis that 'has no time limit': earlier events, including the reasons for the stop and prior interactions, can bear on whether the force was reasonable. The Court expressly did NOT decide whether or how an officer's own creation of the danger factors in.
cases.swat: Your whole operation is on the table: the planning, the approach, the breach and the call-out, not just the trigger press. It lines up with WA's 'totality of the circumstances' definition (RCW 10.120.010(8)), which includes the officer's own actions. That's why sound tactics count legally as well as operationally.
cases.quiz: What did Barnes reject, and what question did it leave open?
cases.answer: It rejected the moment-of-threat doctrine and held that totality has no time limit. It left open how an officer-created danger factors into reasonableness.

cases.name: Scott v. Harris (supplemental)
cases.holding: An officer's attempt to end a dangerous high-speed chase that threatens innocent bystanders does not violate the Fourth Amendment, even when it puts the fleeing motorist at risk of serious injury or death. Where video 'blatantly contradicts' the plaintiff's version, courts view the facts as shown in the video. There is no 'magical on/off switch' test for deadly force; reasonableness is fact-bound.
cases.swat: Federal law is permissive here, but WA law is much tighter: RCW 10.116.060 (pursuit criteria + no shooting at moving vehicles unless the vehicle/occupant is using a deadly weapon) and FWPD MOS 4.1.5. In an interview, show you know the state and agency rules are stricter.
cases.quiz: Would Scott v. Harris alone justify a pursuit in Washington?
cases.answer: No. RCW 10.116.060 imposes statutory pursuit criteria (reasonable suspicion, necessity, risk balance, supervisor oversight) and limits shooting at moving vehicles.

cases.name: Payton v. New York (+ Steagald v. U.S.)
cases.holding: The Fourth Amendment bars a warrantless, nonconsensual entry into a suspect's home to make a routine felony arrest absent exigent circumstances. An arrest warrant founded on probable cause carries limited authority to enter the suspect's OWN dwelling when there is reason to believe the suspect is inside. Steagald: to search a THIRD PARTY's home for the subject of an arrest warrant, you need a search warrant (absent consent or exigency).
cases.swat: This is the legal basis for high-risk arrest-warrant service. Before any entry, confirm whose residence it is and the basis for believing the subject is inside. A third-party address means you need a search warrant.
cases.quiz: The suspect is wanted on a felony arrest warrant and is believed to be at his girlfriend's apartment. What do you need to enter?
cases.answer: A search warrant for her apartment (Steagald), unless there's valid consent or exigency.

cases.name: Brigham City v. Stuart + WA emergency aid (State v. Schultz; State v. Boisselle)
cases.holding: Brigham City: police may enter a home without a warrant when they have an objectively reasonable basis to believe an occupant is seriously injured or imminently threatened with serious injury. Under the Fourth Amendment the officer's subjective motive doesn't matter. Washington, art. I §7: Schultz applied the emergency-aid exception and reaffirmed that it can't be a pretext. Boisselle (2019) restated the test: (1) the officer subjectively believed an emergency required immediate assistance to protect life/property or prevent serious injury, (2) a reasonable person would believe the same, and (3) there was a reasonable basis to associate the need with the place searched. There must be a PRESENT emergency, and a pretextual entry for a criminal investigation is unlawful (evidence suppressed).
cases.swat: WA is stricter than the federal rule because your subjective belief and the absence of pretext both matter. Hasty rescue/emergency entries have to be articulated as genuine aid with a present emergency, documented as such.
cases.quiz: What does Washington require for emergency aid that Brigham City doesn't?
cases.answer: Subjective belief in a present emergency and no pretext for a criminal investigation (Boisselle/Schultz), on top of objective reasonableness and a nexus to the place.

cases.name: Kentucky v. King
cases.holding: The exigent-circumstances rule applies when police do not create the exigency by engaging or threatening to engage in conduct that violates the Fourth Amendment. If officers lawfully knock and announce and occupants then begin destroying evidence, a warrantless entry to prevent that destruction is reasonable. (8-1, Alito, J.; Ginsburg, J., dissenting)
cases.swat: 'Police-created exigency' comes up in knock-and-talks and in surround-and-call-outs that escalate. Ask your legal advisor/DPA how WA courts apply King under art. I §7, which is generally more protective. Don't assume the federal rule controls in WA.
cases.quiz: Under King, when does police conduct defeat a claimed exigency?
cases.answer: When the police created the exigency by engaging or threatening to engage in conduct that violates the Fourth Amendment, e.g. threatening an unlawful entry.

cases.name: Knock-and-announce: Wilson, Richards, Banks, Hudson + State v. Coyle
cases.cite: Wilson v. Arkansas, 514 U.S. 927 (1995); Richards v. Wisconsin, 520 U.S. 385 (1997); U.S. v. Banks, 540 U.S. 31 (2003); Hudson v. Michigan, 547 U.S. 586 (2006); State v. Coyle, 95 Wn.2d 1 (1980)
cases.holding: Wilson: the common-law knock-and-announce principle is part of the Fourth Amendment reasonableness inquiry, but countervailing interests can justify an unannounced entry. Richards: there's no blanket exception for felony drug cases. A no-knock entry requires reasonable suspicion that knocking would be dangerous, futile, or would inhibit the investigation (e.g. destruction of evidence), decided case by case. Banks: waiting 15-20 s before forcing entry was reasonable where cocaine could be destroyed. Hudson: a knock-and-announce violation does not trigger the exclusionary rule. Coyle (WA): RCW 10.31.040 applies whenever police enter without valid permission, not just when they 'break' in. Before a nonconsensual entry officers must announce identity, demand admittance, announce purpose, and be explicitly or implicitly refused. The statute's purposes are to reduce violence, prevent property damage and protect privacy, and exceptions are narrow.
cases.swat: This is the core law of warrant service. Since 2021 (2021 c 320 §8), RCW 10.31.040(2) bars officers from seeking, and courts from issuing, warrants with an express no-knock exception. Whether an on-scene exigency can still excuse compliance is a case-law question, so learn how Valley SWAT trains it (announce, wait time, breach).
cases.quiz: List the four Coyle steps before a nonconsensual entry, and the three purposes of the rule.
cases.answer: Announce identity, demand admittance, announce purpose, be refused (explicitly or implicitly). Purposes: reduce violence, prevent property damage, protect privacy.

policy.title: RCW 10.120: Permissible uses of force (HB 1310 2021, as amended by HB 1735 (2022 c 4) and HB 2037 (2022 c 80))
read: 10.120.010 definitions: 'necessary', 'physical force', 'totality of the circumstances' (includes the officer's own actions), 'de-escalation tactics', 'less lethal alternatives'
10.120.020(1): the 11 lawful purposes for physical force, including (g) executing a search warrant and (i) stopping flight from a Terry stop (added by HB 2037)
10.120.020(2) deadly force: only when necessary to protect against an IMMEDIATE threat of serious physical injury or death (present and apparent ability, opportunity and intent)
10.120.020(3) reasonable care: de-escalate when possible, least force necessary, stop when necessity ends, less-lethal before deadly when possible, carry issued less-lethal
2022 c 4 intent: RCW 10.120.020 is a distinct, more restrictive CIVIL standard and does not abrogate the criminal protections in ch. 9A.16

policy.title: FWPD Manual of Standards Ch. 4: Use of Force (current rev. 05-18-2026), §§4.1.1-4.1.6

Verbal persuasion: one officer talking satisfies the de-escalation/verbalization principle for all officers on scene
4.1.2 definitions (AGMUFP, chokehold, CEW, deadly force, deadly weapon, de-escalation vs. de-escalation tactics)

read: 10.116.020 chokeholds/neck restraints prohibited · 10.116.022 hog-tying prohibited (2024 c 291) and treated as excessive force for RCW 10.93.190

10.116.030 TEAR GAS (CS/CN, not OC) is allowed only to alleviate a present risk of serious harm from a riot, BARRICADED SUBJECT, or HOSTAGE situation. Before use: exhaust alternatives, get SUPERVISOR authorization, ANNOUNCE intent, allow time/space to comply. A riot outside a jail also needs the highest elected official's approval. 10.116.040 military equipment ban. Note that 'grenade' EXCLUDES stun/flash-bang, sting, smoke, tear-gas grenades and blast balls, and 'rifle' means .50 cal+

recipes.name: Overnight protein oats
ing: 200 g rolled oats (½ cup + 2 tbsp per jar)
680 g plain 0% Greek yogurt (¾ cup per jar)
steps: In each jar: 50 g oats, 170 g yogurt, 1 tbsp chia, 100 g berries, cinnamon, splash of milk.
Stir, lid, refrigerate. Good for 4-5 days.

recipes.name: Egg bites (muffin tin)
ing: 1 cup chopped spinach, ½ bell pepper, ¼ onion
steps: Oven 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs and whites, then stir in the veg.
Fill the cups ¾ full and top with cheese.
Bake 20-22 min. Cool, then refrigerate. Keeps 5 days.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan chili-lime chicken
recipes.makes: 5 portions of 7 oz cooked (Tue-Fri dinners + 1 spare)
ing: 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1½ tsp salt
steps: Oven 425°F. Butterfly thick breasts so they cook evenly.
Toss with oil, lime and spices.
Roast 18-22 min to 165°F inside. Rest 5 min, then slice.
Portion into 5 containers with 1½ cups rice + broccoli. Fridge 2 (Tue, Wed), freeze 3 (Thu, Fri, spare).
recipes.portion: Each container: about 7 oz cooked chicken (palm-and-a-half), 1½ cups rice, a big handful of broccoli.

recipes.name: Turkey burrito bowls
ing: Rice (from the batch) + frozen green beans
steps: Brown the turkey and drain.
Add peppers and onion, cook 5 min.
Stir in beans, salsa and seasoning, simmer 10 min.
Bowls: turkey mix + ¾-1 cup rice + green beans. Use leak-proof containers. These are eaten in the patrol car, cold or microwaved.
Fridge 2 (Mon lunch, Tue shift), freeze 4.
recipes.portion: Each bowl: about 1 heaping cup of the turkey mix, ¾–1 cup rice, ½ cup green beans.

recipes.name: Lean beef & bean chili (thermos meal)
recipes.makes: 6 bowls (2 shift meals + 1 dinner + 3 frozen for next week)
ing: 2 cans (15 oz) kidney or pinto beans
2 tbsp chili powder, 1 tbsp cumin, salt
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and garlic.
Add everything else and simmer 30 min.
Portion into 6. Fridge 1, freeze 5.
Shift nights: heat until steaming. Pre-heat the thermos with boiling water for 5 min, dump it, then fill with chili.
recipes.portion: Each container: about 1¾ cups chili (fills a 16–24 oz thermos).

recipes.name: Rice, sweet potatoes & veg
ing: 4 cups dry jasmine rice (≈ 12 cups cooked)
steps: Rice cooker: 4 cups rice.
Roast the sweet potato at 425°F for 30 min.
Roast the broccoli at 425°F for 15-18 min.
Green beans go straight into the turkey bowls frozen (they thaw in the fridge).
recipes.portion: Rice: 1½ cups with each chicken dinner, ¾–1 cup in each turkey bowl. Sweet potato: about 1 cup (200 g) with off-day dinners.

recipes.name: Salmon (cook the day of)
ing: 2 × 6 oz salmon fillets (frozen bag is fine)
steps: Fresh: cook within 2 days (Monday's). Frozen: thaw in the fridge overnight (Saturday's).
Air fryer at 400°F for 8-10 min, or oven at 425°F for 12 min.
recipes.portion: 1 fillet per dinner, with about 1 cup sweet potato and a side salad.

equipment: 2 pots (one for the chili) + 1 big skillet
About 17 leak-proof containers: 5 for chicken dinners, 6 for turkey bowls, 6 for chili
Masking tape + marker to label each container with its DAY
storage: FRIDGE: 2 chicken dinners (Tue, Wed), 2 turkey bowls (Mon lunch, Tue work night), 1 chili (Wed work night), 4 oat jars, 12 egg bites, Monday's salmon.
FREEZER: 3 chicken dinners (Thu, Fri, spare), 4 turkey bowls, 5 chili (Fri, Sun + 3 for next week), Saturday's salmon.
